title: The 1-prompt edit with Claude
creator: Unnamed creator (Srijan upload Video-60622.mp4)
one_liner: Give Claude the tools, a reel whose style you like and your footage; then turn the workflow into a skill.
why_it_matters: This is close to how we already edit your reels, and it shows the missing pieces: word-level transcripts, reference-driven style, and packaging your style as a reusable skill so the next gym or PC reel is one prompt. It's also a lesson in packaging a tutorial: an anti-CTA, a screenshot moment and a full-map ending that drives saves.

big_idea.statement: You can edit without a timeline: give Claude Code a toolset, a reference reel and your raw video, steer it with plain-word feedback, then save the whole thing as a skill.
support: Seven open-source repos cover cutting, transcription, downloading, tracking and motion graphics.
A reference reel tells Claude the style better than any description.
Feedback in plain words replaces dragging clips on a timeline.
'Turn this into a skill' makes the next edit a single prompt.

chapters.title: The hook and the anti-CTA
chapters.summary: The creator rides a trend in the first line: you've probably seen people editing videos with Claude or ChatGPT, so let me show you how. Then comes a trust line that runs against almost every creator tutorial: no DM for resources, everything you need is right here. While other reels gate the links behind 'comment X', this one gives everything on screen, which builds trust and makes people save it.

blocks.text: You've probably seen these videos lately where people are editing their videos with Claude or ChatGPT. Let me show you how to do it.
And I promise no DM for resources, everything you need is right here below.

left.title: Anti-CTA (this reel)
items: 'No DM for resources'
Everything on screen
Builds trust and saves
Stands out from everyone gating links

right.title: Comment-keyword CTA (L01, L02, Rahul)
items: 'Comment X and I'll send it'
Resource sent by DM
Builds comments
Lets you follow up by DM

blocks.text: This is an open clash in the Brain (C1): give it all away (saves, trust) vs gate it behind a comment (comments, DMs). Pick per reel: a full tutorial suits the anti-CTA; a living resource (parts list with live prices) suits the comment CTA.
Trend-riding hook for you: 'You've probably seen people doing the 75 Hard lately. Here's what happened when a desk worker tried week one.'

chapters.title: Setup: Claude Code and seven repos
chapters.summary: Step one is installing Claude Code, switching from the chat to the Code tab, choosing Local and opening a new folder (his is called 'my boss editor'). Next you copy a set of GitHub repositories; he explains GitHub as a place where people share open-source tooling. The repos appear as a table on the red board, and he pauses so you can take a picture, a deliberate save moment.

blocks.title: The seven-repo stack and each one's job
items: FFmpeg: every cut, crop, mix, mute and render
faster-whisper: word-level transcription that every cut is placed against
Whisper: OpenAI's speech model (faster-whisper is a faster runtime for it)
yt-dlp: downloading the reference video
OpenCV (+ contrib): following whoever is talking in a vertical crop
Puppeteer: renders HTML captions and titles to video; took the screenshots
HyperFrames (HeyGen): agent-built motion graphics from HTML

blocks.text: We already run FFmpeg, OpenCV, Python and Claude Code skills. New from this lesson: faster-whisper (word timings for captions and cuts), yt-dlp (reference downloads) and OpenCV's CSRT tracker (auto-follow you in a 9:16 crop), all now installed.

chapters.title: Prompt, reference, footage
chapters.summary: He prompts Claude with a role and the links: you are my short-form editor, here are all the GitHub links to help you do your job. Then he finds an edit he likes (a simple list format) and sends it: can we duplicate this style for a video of mine? Claude processes the reference, he shoots his own video, copies the file path, and Claude edits it in the same format and style. There's no timeline editor involved; corrections are given as plain-word feedback.

blocks.title: A vague brief vs a reference brief
blocks.before: Edit my gym video so it looks good and engaging.
blocks.after: You are my short-form editor. Here's a reel whose style I like [link]. Duplicate this style for my video at [path]: same caption look, same cut rhythm, same SFX.
blocks.why: A reference shows pacing, captions and sound at once; 'looks good' tells Claude nothing. (Applied.)

blocks.text: For you: pick one gym reel and one PC reel whose edits you love, send both with your raw iPhone footage, then give notes like 'cut faster in the warm-up' or 'bigger text on the weight'.

chapters.title: Turn it into a skill
chapters.summary: The last step is the big idea: prompt Claude Code to turn the whole workflow into a skill, so next time it's one prompt. That's how people are doing their 'one prompt edit with Claude'. He closes honestly: it's a lot, but that's probably why people sell courses on it.

blocks.text: So you just prompt Claude code, Hey, turn this into a skill.

chapters.title: How the video is made
chapters.summary: The layout is a talking head on top (him with headphones in a home office) and a red whiteboard-style board below with handwritten numbered steps. The camera zooms and pans across the board to each step and its screenshot. Captions are an uppercase bold white bar of 3–4 words between the two halves. The 'take a picture' pause is a save moment, and the ending pulls back to show the whole board, a full map in one frame that people screenshot or save.

glossary.def: Anthropic's coding agent that can run tools on your computer's files (here: video tools).
A project's code on GitHub; 'copy the repos' means giving Claude the tools' links.
A saved, reusable set of instructions Claude can run again with one prompt.
Editing your video to match the style of a reel you point to.
A transcript with a timestamp for every word, used for captions and precise cuts.
Telling viewers they don't need to comment or DM because everything is in the video.
A moment designed to make viewers save or screenshot (a full list, a 'take a picture' pause).
An OpenCV object tracker that can follow a person to keep them centred in a vertical crop.
